title: an idea is named by its title, and the skill asks what to call it
intention: An idea's commons record is named from the title its author gave it and carries that title, and /idea asks 'what should I call this?' before filing so the title is the author's.
why: Akien 2026-11-23: 'that first few words becomes the title from the point of view of i'm looking at these things marked ideas and it's a number plus some text. that text, in a list of such tickets, IS the title.' And: 'it could even just ask what should i call this? before filing ideas, and that becomes that initial text.' The door already refuses a packet without a title, then names the record from the prose's first seven words and drops the title.
traces_to: Law 1 — the door asks for the title and discards it, so the name is re-derived by hand; Law 5 — the record carries what a reader listing ideas needs now; Law 9 — Akien's correction of the artifact.
how: door.py builds the stem from slug_of(title) and stores title in the record; SKILL.md asks for the name before firing; the charter's input_contract.title says it names the record; the existing proof's prose-slug teeth move to the title; a red-first proof keys the four clauses.

clauses.claim: a capture titled 'cortical column network strategies' lands at <date>-cortical-column-network-strategies.json in the injected commons, and the record's id equals that stem
the record carries `title` byte-identical to the packet's title
prose is still stored byte-identical, and a second capture with the same title on the same day lands at a suffixed stem without overwriting the first
skills/idea/SKILL.md tells the capturer to ask 'what should I call this?' before firing the door, and names that answer as the packet's title

decisions.text: D1: in skills/idea/door.py, _record_path(base, when, title) takes the title and fire passes payload['title']; the stem is <YYYY-MM-DD>-slug_of(title), collision suffix unchanged. The record gains key `title` (stored as given, not normalised). slug_of's docstring says the id is guessable from the title the author chose.

D2: skills/idea/SKILL.md gains a short section before 'Fire the door': ask 'what should I call this?'; the answer is `title`; if Akien says 'you pick', or CC is the author, CC names it and says the name in the same message so he can change it. When the idea arrives mid-tangent it is a bookmark: the name and his words, nothing more. The field list gains `title`.

D3: skills/idea/intention+why.json input_contract.title says the title names the commons record and is the author's answer to 'what should I call this?', instead of 'rides the berth'. Written through the artifact door.

D4: skills/idea/proofs/test_idea_door.py's teeth 'slug is derived from the prose' and 'slug is deterministic' and 'collision suffix keeps the readable stem' assert the title instead: title 'ticket-probe-task-unity' yields stem <date>-ticket-probe-task-unity. Existing records in CairnCommons/ideas/ are not renamed.

D5: red-first proof skills/idea/proofs/test_an_idea_is_named_by_its_title.py with PROVES keyed 1-4, every root injected (trace_root, berths, commons) as test_idea_door.py does; clause 4 reads SKILL.md's text.

measured.saw: the idea door refused a packet without title, then filed Akien's idea as 2026-11-23-well-only-one-box-hex-even-has with no title in the record; it was renamed by hand to 2026-11-23-cortical-column-network-strategies (CairnCommons 63d42b0f9)
measured.how: skills/idea/door.py fired twice in session; record read back; door.py lines 63-110 read
